issues.description: The helper method for appending elements to arrays has inconsistent names between files, which will prevent the project from compiling and confuse students. In the template ArrayHelpers.java the method is named 'appendElement' while Stock.java (and other classes) call 'ArrayHelpers.addElementToArray'. The solution repository uses 'addElementToArray'. This mismatch is structural (method signature/name inconsistency) and blocks students from running or implementing the SealSaloon functionality.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the helper method name across the repository. Rename the method in the template ArrayHelpers.java from 'appendElement' to 'addElementToArray' (matching Stock.java and the solution), or alternatively change calls to use 'appendElement'. Ensure ArrayHelpers provides a public static generic method with the exact name and signature used by Stock.java and other classes.

issues.description: The ArrayHelpers method for appending an element is named inconsistently across artifacts: the template's ArrayHelpers defines appendElement(T[], T) while both the template's Stock class and the solution use addElementToArray(T[], T). This mismatch means students following the template will encounter a missing method (compile error) and must reconcile two different names for the same helper functionality, creating unnecessary cognitive load.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the helper name consistent across artifacts. Rename the template ArrayHelpers.appendElement(...) to addElementToArray(...) (or change Stock to call appendElement everywhere). Best is to align the template with the solution by renaming appendElement to addElementToArray and keeping callers unchanged.
